field.title: Title
fieldHint.internal_note: Pick the column to store verbatim (excluded from Q&A)
fieldHint.title: Suggested column for Title
health.actionAddPhrasingHint: Adds the wording people actually type as a new row that sits alongside the original title and shares the same answer — it does not replace the original title. The original wording is often the real input, and changing it takes a phrasing people really do use out of the index. The new row copies every field of the original and only swaps the title, so tags, validity date and as-of date all come along.
health.actionDisableHint: Rewrites the validity date of these records to a sentinel date in the past so they leave the retrieval set. The data stays in the source file and in the index, its validity has simply passed; if the call was wrong, put that cell back and they return. This requires the tenant to have declared a date dimension with the valid_until role under “Tag dimensions” first, so that the data has somewhere to express “disabled” — without it this action is refused, and it says what is missing. Ticking nothing disables every record this finding involves.
health.actionDismissHint: The only one of the five that touches no data: it records on this row who decided it is not a problem, when, and why. The reason is required — a blank reason means only half of it is on record and the next person has to make the call all over again. Once decided, this finding leaves the open list until the evidence or the confidence really changes.
health.actionMergeHint: Folds the phrasings of the other records into the top of the one you keep and disables the rest without deleting them. One document should carry every phrasing: deleting them all leaves the people who use those phrasings with nothing, while keeping them all eats several of the top sixteen retrieval slots. This action is not offered on QA sets — for direct answers extra phrasings are an asset, not a duplicate, and merging them into one disables the direct answers for those phrasings.
health.actionSupersedeHint: Writes “I have been superseded by this one” onto the superseded records so that recency convergence can follow the pointer to the current version. The value written is the external key of the file the current version lives in, so the granularity is the file: the current version and the superseded records cannot be in the same file, and the file holding the current version must have an external key, or the pointer leads nowhere. This action also requires the tenant to have declared a dimension with the superseded_by role first.
health.actionUndoHint: Rolls back what the last disposal did to the data and puts this finding back on the open list. Undo does not always succeed: it is only well defined while what the disposal wrote is untouched — if the data has been changed since, writing the old value back would wipe out that later change too, so the backend refuses and names the cell that no longer matches. Merge especially: once the same record has been merged a second time by another finding, that one line holds both rounds of phrasings and no single rewrite counts as the inverse. When it is refused, edit the data directly instead of using undo.
health.actionsHint: These are not “mark as read” — each one really changes your data; the single exception is “Not a problem”, which only writes this finding row. They disable or add, never delete; every one of them leaves an audit trail and every one of them can be undone. Which of them this finding offers is decided by the backend, and the page only draws the ones the backend offers.
health.crossDataset: Spans datasets, or belongs to none
health.disableReasonPlaceholder: Why these records should be disabled
health.dismissReasonPlaceholder: Why this is not a problem
health.findingsSortHint: This list is ordered by “check → finding id”, not by impact: retrieval hit counts live in the upstream conversation logs and cannot go into a database sort, and this list is paged — ordering within one page is a fake ordering, and the record on page 2 that is retrieved 50 times a day would never reach page 1. To read by impact, use the overview above.
health.hitChecks: The three that need conversation logs:
health.hitChecksLegend: ran = they were computed this time; not_requested = they were not asked for this time (the stale-but-often-retrieved, never-retrieved and often-asked-never-answered lists keep the previous result, which is not the same as “no problems”); unavailable = they were asked for but the conversation logs could not be fetched, reason on the next line.
health.includeHitChecks: Also recompute the three that need conversation logs (stale but often retrieved / never retrieved / often asked, never answered)
health.includeHitChecksHint: Those three can only be computed by fetching a whole time window of conversation logs from upstream, so they are off by default: when you re-check right after a disposal what changed is the data, and hit statistics do not move within a second. Leaving it on just pays for one upstream fetch per click, and ties “can I re-check” to “is the statistics upstream alive”. The daily full rescan always computes them.
health.intro: The health check pulls out the data that answers, but answers wrongly: duplicated phrasings, numbers that contradict each other, expired answers that are still being retrieved. The check itself only reads — it will not change a single character of your data. What changes data is the disposal actions below, and every one of them leaves an audit trail and can be undone.
health.lastScanNever: This tenant has not run a health check yet. Press “Re-check” above to run the first one; the system also runs one right after data is imported. Until then the overview and the list below are empty — which means “not checked yet”, not “checked and clean”.
health.overviewSortHint: This table is not ordered by how many findings there are. It is ordered by the total number of times the records in each group were retrieved during the time window — one duplicate that has never been retrieved matters far less than one expired answer that is retrieved 50 times a day. Replays from batch regression runs are already excluded from the hit counts, so running a regression will not push the replayed records to the top.
health.overviewTopHintPrefix: Each group lists only its top
health.overviewTopHintSuffix: , and that is not paging: its purpose is to bring the ones worth looking at first in front of you. When a group has more open findings than that, the rest are only visible in the list below.
health.overviewWindowHintSuffix: days rather than 30 by default: upstream aggregates at most 5000 conversations per request, and for a moderately busy tenant a 30-day window is bound to cross that line, which would make the overview impossible to open. When a longer window cannot be opened, the response says that is the reason.
health.partialHint: The two numbers below say which records had which check skipped — they do not say “checked and clean”. On the findings list those two look identical: the list can only show findings that were computed, never “this check was not run at all”.
health.recordSourceHint: The marker in front of a title says what that title is, and the three are not the same kind of thing: [Row] = the title cell of a row-wise import (merging writes exactly that string into the source file); [Whole document] = one file imported from a folder, where the title is its original filename, not its content; [What people asked] = a group of questions that got no answer, which was never a record in the knowledge base to begin with. The id after it is the value the disposal actions actually send.
health.recordTitleBlank: (the title cell of this record is empty)
health.recordUnavailable: (the title of this record cannot be read)
health.reopenedHint: A disposed finding only comes back to the list when the premise of the original decision changed — that is, the evidence computed this time, or the confidence, is not the same as when the decision was made. If the premise has not changed, re-checking only updates “Last seen” and does not push it back. An undone disposal also lands here. Below is the reason the system wrote down, including the evidence as it stood at the time of the disposal.
health.reopenedTitle: This one was disposed of, and came back to the open list
health.scanExactMatchOnly: Records too long to compare, matched only character for character:
health.scanExactMatchOnlyHint: For records over the length limit, the near-duplicate check only decided whether they are character-for-character identical this time: the same document uploaded twice is still caught, but “almost the same two documents” was not compared. The limit exists because similarity is a pairwise comparison — a single pair of long documents takes tens of seconds, and a few dozen monthly reports sharing one template would make the whole scan never finish, which stops every check at once and is worse than one check under-reporting.
health.scanFailedHint: That attempt failed, so the numbers below are still from the last check that succeeded, not from the most recent one. A failure never overwrites the last successful result — overwriting it would take “which files were not looked at that time” away as well. This block disappears after the next successful check.
health.scanFailedTitle: The most recent check did not finish
health.scanRecordLimitHint: When “Records read” goes over the per-run limit, nothing is checked and no finding is written at all: near-duplicate detection compares every pair, and past the limit the check would run longer than anyone waits — while “scanned half of it” and “scanned all of it” look exactly the same on the list. The limit after the slash is given by the backend; it is not a number written into the page.
health.scanSlotless: Records with no field slots, where the two tag checks do not apply:
health.scanSlotlessHint: A whole document imported from a folder has no field slots — column mapping only exists for row-wise imports, and there is no path that could write tags onto them. So the tag-gap and missing-as-of checks exclude them: these records will not show up on the list for being untagged, and that does not mean they are tagged. To bring this content under dimension filtering, import it row by row instead.
health.scanTriggerLegend: manual = somebody pressed “Re-check” above; import = the run that follows a data import; daily = the scheduled full rescan (only that one always computes the three checks that need conversation logs). “The last check was 20 minutes ago” does not mean the same thing when somebody just pressed the button as when the scheduler ran it.
health.supersedeCurrent: Which one is the current version
health.supersedeRestHint: The records not chosen as the current version are the ones it supersedes.
health.uncoveredCount: Listed in this table / not looked at in total:
health.uncoveredCountHint: When the two sides of the slash differ, the table below has been truncated: the first number is how many rows this table can show, the second is how many files were not looked at this time. The per-reason counts beside it are computed over all of them and are not affected by the truncation — for the group that got cut, that number is the only thing left to see.
health.uncoveredHint: These files are not part of this check — their content will not show up in any of the checks. They are listed because a missed problem is worse than a false one: a file nobody has looked at looks exactly like “clean” on the list.
health.uncoveredNone: Every file was looked at this time
health.uncoveredTitle: Files not looked at this time
health.undoReasonPlaceholder: Why this disposal should be rolled back

qa.exportFullDetailHint: Full detail adds three worksheets — every step, the full output of every tool call, and the full text of every source card
qa.exportWithHeaderHint: With this on, the first CSV row is no longer the column names — existing downstream parsers will misalign
qaSet.intro: A QA set is a collection of question-answer pairs: when a question exactly matches an entry's question, its answer is returned verbatim without AI rephrasing. Choose which QA sets take part in direct answering under Conversation Settings ▸ QA direct answer.
qaSet.previewFailed: Failed to read Excel columns; please check the file format
regression.abortedMeaning: This is not a complete regression run: only the cases listed below were actually replayed; for the rest, whether they regressed simply was not measured this time.
regression.addCaseIntro: Try “Create case from a Q&A record” first — assertions derived from a real record are more reliable than hand-written ones. Manual creation is for questions that have not been asked yet.
regression.aiTurnNotSent: On replay only the user half of each preceding turn is sent: the AI half is regenerated upstream (GufoRAG continues a conversation by chatroom id only — there is no field that can inject earlier AI replies).
regression.assertionCodeHint: One assertion carries exactly one code. To require two codes, write two assertions.
regression.assertionCriteriaHint: The criteria text enters the prompt on every evaluation (one regression run is dozens of answers × several criteria each). Criteria length limit:
regression.assertionGate: At least one deterministic assertion is required. A subjective score never affects pass/fail — a case with only subjective scoring always passes and always lands in “Unchanged” in the baseline comparison, which means it can never detect a regression.
regression.assertionIdentityHint: Pick one. `document_id` is stable addressing — renaming the file will not turn the case red for no reason.
regression.assertionPatternHint: Only rules from the platform list — hand-written regular expressions are not accepted, because that would store an arbitrary pattern in the case and run it on the server on every execution.
regression.assertionPrefixHint: Leave empty to only require “has a link”. Do not type an empty string as “no prefix restriction” — every URL matches an empty prefix, so the assertion degrades into “is there a link” while you believe you restricted the domain.
regression.bucketFixedWhy: These failed in the baseline run and pass now.
regression.bucketJudgeDrift: Judge drift (subjective scores can no longer be measured)
regression.bucketJudgeDriftWhy: The deterministic verdicts of these cases really did not change, so they genuinely belong in “Unchanged” — but this run lost their subjective scores entirely. Without this block the report would read “nothing changed” while in fact this batch has no subjective score at all. It tracks the transition between “scored” and “not scored”, not how high the score is.
regression.bucketNotCompared: Not compared (only one side has a result)
regression.bucketNotComparedWhy: Only one side has a result for these cases, so whether they regressed was not measured this time — that is not “unchanged”. Folding them into Unchanged would let a run that aborted halfway report “0 regressed”.
regression.bucketRegressedWhy: This is what the whole report is for: these passed in the baseline run and fail now — they are what this change broke.
regression.bucketUnchangedWhy: The deterministic verdict is the same in both runs (including cases that failed both times). This block excludes “not compared” and “judge drift” — those two have their own blocks above.
regression.caseQuestionBlank: . Whitespace-only questions (including full-width spaces) are rejected, so a case that fails on every replay never gets stored.
regression.contextTurnsSentHint: (only the user half is replayed; 0 here means no preceding turn could be carried over, which is normal rather than a fault — each production Q&A gets its own chatroom)
regression.driftAvailableNow: Not scored last time, scored now
regression.driftUnavailableNow: Scored last time, not scored now
regression.effectiveBaselineMissing: The baseline run did not record what it actually used, so “where do the two runs differ” cannot be answered this time — do not read the table below as “the two runs used the same settings”.
regression.effectiveDiffCountSuffix: setting(s) differ — at 0 the two runs used the same configuration, so a regression was not caused by the settings.
regression.effectiveIntro: This is the configuration that was actually sent to the answering engine, recorded when the run started — not a fresh read of the profile (if the profile has changed since, this still shows what really ran). Rows marked “From the profile” took whatever the profile under test had at that moment; rows marked “Set for this run” are the ones deliberately changed.
regression.effectiveRestHint: This table only lists the settings that “Run this suite” can change. The rest of the profile (content policy, output rules, direct QA answers, tag filtering…) always comes from the profile — that endpoint structurally cannot touch them, and sending one is rejected as an unknown override field.
regression.exportColumns: Seven columns: case / expectation / actual answer / pass or fail / cited documents / judge score / why it failed. “Pass or fail” is literally one of two words, with the failure detail in its own column (in a downstream pivot table every distinct detail sentence stuffed into a status column becomes a new status value); “cited documents” lists the documents actually cited, writes “(no hits)” when there were none and states the total when the list is capped — a blank cell would read as “this question hit nothing”.
regression.exportPartialHint: Aborted or still-running executions can be exported too, but the CSV only contains the cases that finished — its last row states how many rows there are and why the run stopped. Do not read it as “the whole suite ran”.
regression.exportPartialPrefix: This execution was aborted; the exported CSV only contains
regression.exportPartialSuffix: case results, and its last row states the row count and the abort reason — do not read it as “the whole suite ran”.
regression.fromLog: Create case from a Q&A record
regression.fromLogContextCost: Off by default. Every preceding turn is a real Q&A on every execution (one chatbot call, one Q&A quota unit). Exceeding the limit rejects the whole request instead of keeping only the most recent turns — truncation would produce a case that looks complete but lost its earliest context.
regression.fromLogIncludeContextOn: Follow this record's preceding-turn chain and carry the whole conversation into the case
regression.fromLogIntro: The question, the preceding turns and the assertions are all derived by the backend from that record: if it had hits, the expectation is “still cites the same primary source”; if it had none, “still honestly answers not found”. When nothing can be derived, no empty-assertion case is created.
regression.fromLogNeedsHistory: It is the conversation id shown on each row of the History page. Besides the settings permission, this endpoint also requires the “Q&A history” capability — it reads questions, answers and source document names.
regression.fromLogRefuse: Two kinds of “cannot derive” must be read differently: this record is unsuitable (no answer, blocked by policy, too many preceding turns) — pick another record or create the case manually; or the upstream data is broken (unexpected hit-list shape, first hit has no document identity) — that is not something you did wrong, please report it.
regression.hitsWhy: Each block below gains two columns, “Cited in baseline” and “Cited in this run”: the most common cause of a regression is “it used to cite A and now cites B”, and that is only visible with both sides next to each other. Every stored hit keeps the document identity and where it came from, never the full text, and there is a per-case cap — when the list is capped the cell states the real total, so do not read it as “only these documents were cited”.
regression.intro: A suite is a set of questions that carry their own assertions. One execution replays the whole suite, judges each case pass or fail, and compares the result against a previous run — the regressed ones are exactly what this change broke.
regression.judgeAvgBasePrefix: The subjective average covers only the
regression.judgeAvgBaseSuffix: could not be judged and were not counted as 0, which would have dragged the average down. Cases without a judge score:
regression.judgeNoThreshold: The subjective score never affects pass/fail and has no threshold: a low score does not turn a case red. Only “has criteria but was not scored” is flagged as not judged.
regression.limitContextTurnsWhy: . Every turn costs one Q&A quota unit on every execution.
regression.limitsWhy: Anything over a limit is rejected outright; the first few cases are never run on their own — that would be a report that looks all green. Split large suites into several suites.
regression.llmEffortUnsupported: This product cannot send a thinking depth to this model: if the profile's judging group has one set, the judge cannot be built either (again this only affects the subjective score, not the answers).
regression.llmFromCatalog: The choices are exactly the models this tenant is allowed to use; this field does not take free text — a typo would only be caught after you press Start, and that wait is already spent.
regression.llmProviderUnsupported: This model's provider is outside the range this product can build: when the profile's judging group has no model of its own the judge inherits this run's model and cannot be built, so every subjective assertion in this run comes back as “judge did not finish”. The answers themselves are still produced by the answering engine.
regression.notComparedDetail: Why it could not be compared
regression.overMemoryPrefix: For these cases the preceding turns plus the question exceed the upstream memory window, so the earliest turns never reach the model:
regression.overrideInheritHint: This field is not sent with the run; it uses whatever the profile under test has at that moment.
regression.overrideScope: Only fields with “Set a value for this run” ticked are sent with the execution; the rest are left out of the request and the backend uses whatever the profile under test has at that moment — so ticking nothing means the run measures the profile's current behaviour. Inherited fields deliberately do not prefill the profile's current values: that would be a copy taken when the page loaded, and it would keep stating stale values after the profile is changed elsewhere. What this run actually used is shown under “What this run actually used” in the report afterwards. Overrides are written only to a temporary config for this execution that is deleted afterwards — the live profile is never touched. “Knowledge retrieval” is not an override; it selects which profile is under test.
regression.overrideSummaryPrefix: Settings explicitly specified for this run:
regression.overrideSummarySuffix: of them; everything else uses whatever the profile under test has at that moment — specify zero and the run measures the profile's current behaviour.
regression.overrideThisRun: Set a value for this run
regression.quotaWarnPrefix: Running the suite consumes Q&A quota: this run is expected to consume
regression.quotaWarnSuffix: units (each preceding turn and the question itself is one real Q&A). Quota already consumed by an aborted run is not refunded.
regression.runProgressPrefix: So far this run has completed
regression.runProgressUnscoredSuffix: cases (a judge assertion exists but no score came back — that is a failure, not “this case has no subjective score”)
regression.sampleTotalOnlyTraditional: Only takes effect in traditional search mode. When the chat mode comes from the profile, this page cannot tell whether this field will be used at all — check “What this run actually used” in the report afterwards.
regression.typeDirectionIs: Dimension value of the cited document
regression.typeNotMatches: Must not match a platform rule
serviceKey.ackOnce: I understand the secret is shown only once, and I have its destination ready.
serviceKey.intro: Machine credentials are for callers that are not people — today only the nightly data health scan. A credential is not a platform master key: each one carries a single scope, endpoints outside that scope always refuse it, and on any endpoint that expects a signed-in identity it does not constitute an identity at all. Issuing and revoking require a platform administrator; auditors can read the inventory.
serviceKey.issueBeforeWarn: Once you press issue, the secret is shown this one time. The system keeps only its SHA-256 hash, so closing this page, reloading it, or pressing “I have saved it” puts the secret out of reach for good — there is no “show it again”, only revoke and re-issue. Have its destination ready before you press issue.
serviceKey.issueDestinationHint: In production the destination is the product-health-scan-key secret in Secret Manager: copy it with the button below and paste it there. Do not print the secret in a terminal — that leaves it in shell history, in the argument list visible to ps, and in any screen recording.
serviceKey.listStoredHint: This table can never return a secret: the system keeps only the SHA-256 hash plus the last four characters for identification. If you cannot tell which credential a row is, go by the name and those four characters; if they still do not match anything, revoke it and issue a new one rather than guessing.
serviceKey.name: What it is for
serviceKey.nameHint: During rotation you have to be able to tell which row belongs to which consumer, so name the consumer (for example “nightly health-scan CronJob”). The name grants nothing; it only decides whether this table still makes sense to you later.
serviceKey.none: There are no valid machine credentials. The schedule needs one to run — without it the job fails every day, and that failure is written only into the job’s log.
serviceKey.plainOnce: This is the only time this credential’s secret is shown. Leave or reload this page and all that is left on screen are the last four characters; the system itself holds only the hash, so nobody can read it back.
serviceKey.revokeHint: Revoking is a soft delete and takes effect immediately (unlike a sign-in session, which waits out its lifetime): the row stays, because “this credential existed, and who revoked it when” is a fact auditing has to be able to look up — and while the row is there that secret can never be brought back. Revoked rows are hidden by default; tick “include revoked” to see the history.
serviceKey.rotateHint: Zero-downtime rotation: issue the new credential first (one scope may hold several valid credentials at once), put it into Secret Manager and let the consumer pick it up, then watch “last used” — when the old one stops advancing, nobody is using it any more, and only then do you revoke it. Forcing one credential per scope would leave a gap in the middle of every rotation during which the schedule is mute and nobody notices.
serviceKey.scopeHint: The scope decides which endpoints this credential may call, compared for exact equality — a value outside the list is refused at issue time. The available scopes and what each one covers are in the table below.
serviceKey.scopesHint: This table is the endpoint’s own value set, not a copy kept by this page. A scope decides what a credential may do, rather than merely whether one was presented — a health-scan credential is refused on the tenant list, the audit log, timezone writes and on issuing another credential.
settings.agentToolsIntro: Tools the Agent can call in Agent mode: built-in tools, bound glossary tables, and MCP Servers registered on the platform.
settings.answerabilityCriteriaPlaceholde: Extra criteria (appended after the built-in grounding criteria)...
settings.answerabilityEnable: Enable answerability gate (honestly say no when material is insufficient)
settings.answerabilityIntro: When the collected or retrieved material is insufficient to answer, honestly say so instead of fabricating an ungrounded answer.
settings.assignedSkillsHint: Assigned skills become tools the agent can call; it decides when to use them from their "what it does" description.
settings.attributionDimensionsIntro: Pick the fields used to attribute answers. The order here is the column order in reports and exports. Nothing selected means no attribution — conversation details and export files will not grow attribution columns.
settings.builtinToolsHint: All on = all enabled; only some on = only the enabled tools are available; all off = every built-in tool is disabled.
settings.confirmDeleteTagDimension: Deleting this also takes the whole vocabulary with it, and values already tagged on documents become values outside the vocabulary. Are you sure you want to delete
settings.conversationSettingsIntro: Set every conversation behavior for all three configurations (Config 1/2/3) in one place. Each knob is stored per configuration; switch configuration above. Which one the frontend Q&A uses by default is a shared setting.
settings.copyConfigGroupDatasetBinding: Answer index binding: answer indexes, QA direct-answer indexes
settings.copyConfigGroupGlossary: Glossary binding: glossaries this config uses at runtime
settings.copyConfigGroupPolicy: Compliance: blocked words, denied topics, blocked input message, blocked output message
settings.copyConfigGroupPrompts: Prompts: five system prompt layers (chatroom / product / intent / respond / agent), persona, response format, welcome message
settings.copyConfigGroupRetrieval: Retrieval & generation: model, temperature, sample counts (total / selected), data source ratio, knowledge mode, QA direct-answer mode & criteria, reranking, memory turns, suggested questions, auto-title (first turn only), timezone, search mode & agent iteration cap, citations, Langfuse tracing, dataset tiers & per-tier intent, field display labels
settings.copyConfigGroupTools: Tools: built-in tool enablement & overrides, MCP server selection
settings.copyConfigProductionWarning: The target config is the one currently serving public frontend Q&A — this copy will directly change public-facing behavior. Confirm the source config is appropriate for external use first.
settings.coverageGapsIntro: Lists the questions asked most often in this period that retrieved no document at all. Greetings and small talk are listed as-is with no keyword guessing; which ones to drop is yours to name, one by one.
settings.draftSaveHint: Saving will automatically create a new version without overwriting the old one
settings.excludedPersistentTitle: Permanent · whole tenant (applied to everyone's report)
settings.excludedSessionTitle: This query only · cleared on reload
settings.fieldNamingDescSuffix: field slots for this profile (the display name used by this profile)
settings.filterableDateRangePrefix: Values in a date dimension must fall between
settings.filterableDateRangeSuffix: : the retrieval engine stores dates as a 64-bit nanosecond count, and anything past that overflows to the other end of time. An out-of-range value can still be stored and still matches exact comparison, but every filter that uses a date range will miss that document — at query time it is simply gone, with no error message. If what you mean is "valid forever", leave the cell blank and the system fills in a value that never expires.
settings.gapClassifyLimitReached: The per-request classification limit has been reached: the distinct questions beyond it were not sent for classification this time and are listed as they are under "not sent for classification" below. The budget is spent on the most-asked questions, so what stays outside is the tail that was only asked once or twice.
settings.gapDimensionHint: Picking a dimension is what sends each question off to be classified (once per question, results cached). Date dimensions and dimensions with an empty vocabulary are not listed — they have no controlled vocabulary to group by. Without grouping no model is called at all and every question lands in "not sent for classification".
settings.gapKindOutOfScopeHint: The classifier confidently decided these questions do not fall under any code (mostly greetings and small talk). Either widen the vocabulary, or use "Exclude" on each row to take them out.
settings.gapKindUnclassifiedHint: These questions were never sent for classification: either no grouping dimension was given, or they fell outside the per-request classification limit (the budget is spent on the most-asked questions). This is a boundary of the report, not a property of the data.
settings.gapKindUndeterminedHint: The classifier ran but reached no conclusion — this covers both "the model said it was unsure" and "the classifier is broken across the board", which cannot be told apart at the type level, so this report does not pretend to tell them apart either. When this row is unusually large, go read the backend error log — it does not mean "these questions are all small talk".
settings.glossaryMgmtIntro: Glossary tables let the QA agent look up term definitions and aliases; "when to consult" is the tool description the LLM uses to decide when to check this table.
settings.glossaryNormalizeRegexPlacehold: e.g. [-.\s] to strip separators; no quantifiers (* + ? {})
settings.groundingScoreFloorNote: This one cannot be left empty (default 0.5): it is only a ticket taken before the judgment, and the LLM judgment always runs while the gate is on — so a floor that blocks nothing only costs one extra judgment and never produces a wrong answer. Deliberately unlike the QA direct answer floor, which may be empty.
settings.groupMgmtIntro: Groups are permission groups: capabilities are defined on the group, and a user inherits them by joining (the union across all their groups). Datasets belong to a group, and write access follows group membership.
settings.impersonateDesc: Log in as this member to help troubleshoot issues. For support and debugging use only.
settings.internalNoteHint: This column is purely a product-side record: it is never searched, never reaches the AI’s reference material, and cannot be used as a statistics or filter dimension. It is stored verbatim on import — not even HTML-to-Markdown conversion is applied.
settings.manageMembersHint: Select the members to include in this group
settings.mcpServersHint: A Server marked (inactive) can still be added to this profile, but it will not be called until the platform enables it.
settings.mcpServersIntro: MCP Servers let the Agent connect to external tools. Registering runs the given command on the Agent host — a high-privilege operation, so only platform admins may manage them; tenants can only select registered Servers in conversation settings.
settings.modeApplicabilityHint: Conversation mode decides which fields below take effect; fields for the other mode do not appear.
settings.outputPipelineOrderHint: The three stages cannot be reordered. The compliance gate always runs last, so text rewritten by these rules still has to pass it — output rules can never become a way around the gate.
settings.outputPipelineStage1: Output replacements: swap each matched alias for the text you gave (configured on the Content policy tab).
settings.outputPipelineStage2: Output rules: the rules on this tab, applied to the text that output replacements produced.
settings.outputPipelineStage3: Compliance gate: the output action of each policy topic plus word filtering (configured on the Content policy tab).
settings.outputReplacementsHint: After generating the answer, replace any matched alias with the given text; ${0}=matched text, use ${name} for named regex groups, $$ for a literal $. Regex must not contain quantifiers. Applies in both conversation modes.
settings.outputRuleCaseOperandHintPrefix: With “equals code” enter one code; with “in code list” separate them with commas, up to
settings.outputRuleCasesHintPrefix: Matched top to bottom; the first case that holds wins, otherwise the default value is used. Up to
settings.outputRuleCategoryDuplicate: Duplicate code: only the last row takes effect — delete the duplicate.
settings.outputRuleCategoryHintPrefix: The dimension slot and the per-code caps have to be set together; with only one of them the overrides never take effect. Up to
settings.outputRuleConstDefaultHint: Required: used on the turns where no case holds. It cannot be left blank.
settings.outputRuleConstNameHint: The prompt has to carry a placeholder of the same name (no surrounding spaces, no braces in the name itself), for example
settings.outputRuleConstantRouteDesc: The prompt only carries a placeholder; this rule fills in the actual value from the intent decision made for this turn, and falls back to the default value when no case holds.
settings.outputRuleFlagConflictDesc: When a topic has several equally current records, a separate paragraph is added after the answer listing each one’s as-of date and source name, and saying that these may not agree — rather than picking one. That paragraph cannot say what each one claims: output processing runs without AI and has only the dates and source names, so summarising what those records say would be a statement with nothing behind it. One document split into several chunks counts once; if fewer than two sources have a readable date and name, the paragraph is not added.
settings.outputRuleLinkAnchorDesc: Turns bare URLs, angle-bracket URLs and HTML anchor tags into markdown links [text](url). Answers are rendered as markdown, so an HTML anchor tag left in place shows up on screen as a literal tag.
settings.outputRuleLinkHideUrlDesc: When the visible text is exactly the URL, replaces it with the host plus the last path segment; the URL itself stays as the link target.
settings.outputRuleLinkMaxDesc: Beyond the cap, keeps the first few links and leaves only the visible text of the rest.
settings.outputRuleListMarkerDesc: Rewrites line-leading 1), (1) and 一、 into 1., keeping the original number and indentation (no renumbering).
settings.outputRuleMaxBulletsDesc: Beyond the cap, only reports a violation; it does not drop any bullet.
settings.outputRuleMaxCharsDesc: Beyond the cap, only reports a violation and never truncates the answer — cutting at a sentence boundary drops the proviso that makes the answer correct. The cap can be overridden per code of this turn's intent decision.
settings.outputRuleStateAsOfDesc: When the data an answer cites carries an as-of date, a note like “(this information is as of 2024-11-30)” is appended to the closing sentence. With several cited records the oldest one wins — once a passage cites an older record it only holds good up to that day, and printing the most recent date would vouch for the part that has already gone stale. The note joins the end of the last prose line; if that line is a table, list, quote, heading or code fence it starts its own paragraph instead of being swallowed by it.
settings.outputRuleStripBracketTagDesc: Removes bracketed tags at the start of a line. The list below says which ones; brackets outside the list are kept as they are.
settings.outputRuleStripHeadingDesc: Removes markdown heading lines and bold mini-heading opening lines; when such a line still carries content, only the marker goes, not the whole line.
settings.outputRuleStripLeadPhraseDesc: Removes boilerplate at the start of the answer. The list below says which ones; when several match, the longest one wins.
settings.outputRuleStripLeadYesnoDesc: Removes a standalone “Yes.” / “No.” sentence at the start of the answer; only a whole sentence goes, never half of one.
settings.outputRuleValuesHintSuffix: characters; leading and trailing spaces are stripped.
settings.outputRulesIntro: Deterministic post-processing (no AI) applied to the whole answer after it is generated and before it reaches the compliance gate. The order of the three output stages is fixed by the platform and cannot be changed.
settings.outputRulesMaxHint: A profile holds only so many rules; once the cap is reached “Add rule” is disabled — delete one to make room.
settings.outputRulesStreamingCostOff: No output rule is enabled, so answers still appear word by word. Enabling any single rule switches this profile to showing the whole answer at once when generation finishes, with nothing in between (a rule can only judge the answer as a whole).
settings.outputRulesStreamingCostOn: Output rules are on: answers for this profile no longer appear word by word. A rule can only judge the answer as a whole (total links, list numbering, length), so the answer appears all at once when generation finishes, with nothing shown in between. Disable every rule to get word-by-word output back.
settings.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters
settings.pleaseEnterSkillDescription: What it does + when to use it
settings.pleaseEnterTagCodeDesc: What kind of question counts as this one; this sentence goes into the intent-classification prompt
settings.pleaseEnterTagCodeLabel: A name for people to read
settings.pleaseEnterTagDimensionDesc: What this dimension is about; this sentence goes into the intent-classification prompt
settings.pleaseEnterWhenToConsult: Describe when this table should be consulted
settings.policyIntro: Define sensitive topics and word filters: block, record, or ignore matching input/output, and set the refusal message shown to the user when blocked.
settings.policyWordFiltersHint: One word per line, or comma-separated.
settings.qaDirectIntro: When a question exactly matches a QA set's question, return that answer verbatim without AI rephrasing; judge mode adds one LLM decision.
settings.qaDirectScoreFloorDep: Empty = not calibrated: with adjudication on it means no pre-filtering and everything goes to the judge; with adjudication off it means only the “normalized exact match” layer is used, which is a safe setup. But when the mode is “exact match” and reranking is off on the “Generation” tab, a floor must not be set — only the raw retrieval score is left and that is not a calibratable scale, so saving is rejected. Two ways out: turn reranking on (the score then comes from the reranker), or leave this empty.
settings.reasoningGroupIntentDesc: Analyzes the language, keywords, time range, and filename intent of the user's input (the intent-detection stage of traditional search mode).
settings.reasoningGroupJudgeDesc: Judges whether retrieved material is sufficient to answer (the answerability grounding gate and tiered-retrieval IsAnswerable), QA direct-answer adjudication, and content-policy topic adjudication.
settings.reasoningGroupRecommendDesc: The follow-up question suggestions and the chat-room title produced after each answer. This group runs every round (suggested questions are on by default), making it the only one of the five that costs money on every turn — pointing it at a smaller model has the most impact.
settings.reasoningGroupSkillDesc: The tool loop and reply inside a tenant's custom skill (a skill's output is a tool result fed back to the main agent).
settings.reasoningGroupToolsDesc: In agent chat mode, the reasoning for choosing and calling tools each round (excludes final answer generation).
settings.reasoningGroupsIntro: Each internal LLM call other than the main answer (what the user finally sees) can use its own model and reasoning depth. Leave empty to inherit the main model / minimal thinking.
settings.recencyWindowNote: The "recent data window" is not a switch that takes effect on its own: it only appears when intent classification decides the question is asking for the latest data, and when the classification is inconclusive the whole condition is discarded together with the window. The reason is that the window is the only predicate with no "untagged" branch — keeping it would filter out documents that have no publication date at all.
settings.rerankerScaleNote: Each reranker uses a different score scale, so switching reranker means recalibrating the score floor on the “QA direct answer” tab and the one on the answerability gate. Current scale:
settings.scoreScaleRecalibrate: The score scale just changed (you changed the reranker model, the rerank switch, or the data source ratio). This floor was calibrated against the old scale — recalibrate it: a number from a 1–5 scale moved onto a 0–1 scale becomes a condition that never blocks anything.
settings.skillAllowedToolsHint: Only the checked tools can be used by this skill; anything unchecked simply does not exist at run time — it is not "disallowed", it is unreachable.
settings.skillDescriptionHint: Describe both what this skill does and when it should be used — this is the only thing the agent uses to decide whether to call it, so a vague description means it never triggers.
settings.skillInputSchemaHint: A JSON Schema describing what the agent must pass when calling this tool (top level must be an object; document_ids, indexes and dsl are not allowed). Leave empty and the agent calls it with a single natural-language task.
settings.skillInstructionsHint: Loaded only when the skill is called, as its system prompt. If the steps must run in order, spell them out here.
settings.skillMaxIterationsHint: How many rounds this skill's inner loop may run (1-20). Too low and it gets cut off before finishing.
settings.skillMgmtIntro: A skill is a reusable capability pack: instructions plus a set of tools. The agent decides on its own when to call it, based on "what it does". Agent mode only.
settings.skillNameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 1-64 characters; cannot start or end with a hyphen, and no consecutive hyphens. This is also the tool name the agent sees.
settings.skillNestedHint: Referenced skills become tools this skill can call. Cycles are not allowed; nesting depth is capped at 3.
settings.tagCodeHint: Codes go verbatim into the retrieval condition, so they must not contain , ' " \ * ? (those get rewritten or cut somewhere along "import matching → DSL string → upstream matching"). Two codes differing only in case or full/half width cannot coexist either — the matcher cannot tell them apart, while retrieval can only send one of the two spellings.
settings.tagCoverageScanHint: “No content found” and “files that cannot be enumerated” do not mean “not tagged” — they mean “not known yet”, so they are listed separately and excluded from the denominator; counting them as tagged would overstate coverage. Coverage is a report on how much is tagged, not the test for whether filtering can be enabled: that is decided by “every document carries this column” — see the retrieval filter section below.
settings.tagDimensionsIntro: A tag dimension declares one physical filter slot as a business dimension and gives it a controlled vocabulary; at query time intent classification picks the codes and compiles them into a retrieval filter. The engine itself knows no business codes — it only knows "this field equals this string".
settings.tagFilterBlockedHint: This table has nothing to do with a dimension’s kind: “unset” is now a sentinel value written at import time and all three kinds can express it, so how much is tagged does not affect whether documents get dropped. The only remaining gap is “this file does not have the column at all” — that is a structural fact, and only re-importing (or importing row by row) fixes it.
settings.tagFilterBlockedTitle: The dimensions below are not carried by every document yet; turning filtering on now would silently exclude those files
settings.tagFilterCoverageWarnBlocked: Some files have not written this column into the index (the dimension did not exist when they were imported, or they were imported as a folder). Turning filtering on in this state silently excludes those files — the filter matches “this column equals a code or equals unset”, and those files do not have the column at all. Agent mode has no no-result relaxation ladder, so a filtered-out document is really gone and users just experience it as “some data cannot be found”. That is exactly why this switch is off by default.
settings.tagFilterCoverageWarnOk: Every document currently carries this column, so filtering can be turned on. Empty cells were written as “Unset” at import time and the filter matches them too, so how much is tagged does not affect whether documents get dropped. Only one thing to watch from here: a folder import never has field slots, so importing a new batch that way loses the column again — switch that batch to a row-by-row import to bring it back.
settings.tagFilterFixNotMapped: Re-importing once adds the column, and empty cells are filled in with “Unset” automatically.
settings.tagFilterFixWholeFile: A folder import has no field slot to carry this column: either re-import that batch row by row, or do not filter on this dimension.
settings.tagFilterIntro: Once enabled, a question is first classified into business dimensions and the result is compiled into a retrieval filter for the engine. When the classification is inconclusive the whole condition is discarded (the recency window with it) — it never degrades into a looser condition.
settings.tagFilterNotMapped: The dimension did not exist at import time, so that column never reached the index
settings.tagFilterWholeFile: Imported as a folder — the whole file is one document, so there are no field slots
settings.tagKindHint: Single = one of several; multi = several at once; date = compared by magnitude. Date slots (date2/date3) can only be the date type, and no other slot can be — a mismatched pair is rejected upstream on every single search.
settings.tagRoleHint: Roles are what the engine's built-in mechanisms look for: valid_until/as_of only on date dimensions, fact_topic/superseded_by only on single-value dimensions. A mismatch raises no error — the mechanism simply skips this dimension, so the settings page looks fine while that mechanism never took effect at all.
settings.tagSlotHint: Only the slots product declares to the retrieval engine as custom filter fields (note1–note10, date2, date3) can carry a dimension; DSL references to built-in slots are rejected upstream. One slot can hold only one dimension, and one role can be assigned to only one dimension.
settings.tagVocabularyIntro: The vocabulary is this dimension's legal value range: on import the column only accepts codes from the list, and intent classification only picks from the same list. For a single/multi dimension whose vocabulary is empty, import rejects every non-empty value in that column.
settings.toolRequiresUnmet: Checked, but will not take effect this round — missing prerequisite:
settings.trySkillHint: Temporarily assigns this skill to the test profile and runs one agent turn; your live profiles are untouched. The flow below shows how it actually got called.
settings.trySkillPlaceholder: Ask something that should trigger this skill
settings.untaggedFilesHint: This list and the coverage figure come from the same scan, shown two ways: coverage says how many are still missing, this says which ones. Documents with no indexed content are not counted as untagged (they are not yet synced, not unlabelled), so they are not listed below — that number is shown separately in the section above.
settings.weeklyRetrievalTrend: Retrieval count over the last 4 weeks
share.expiresDaysHint: A share link can be opened without signing in; setting a number of days makes it expire on its own.
share.rateLimited: This share link is still valid — it is just being accessed too often right now. Please try again in a moment.

tool.analyze_user_intent.desc: Breaks the user question down into structured information such as language, full question and keywords. Not needed in ordinary conversations.
tool.analyze_user_intent.example.descrip: Call this when the user asks several things at once and they have to be split apart before being handled one by one.
tool.analyze_user_intent.example.extraPr: Answer each item in order after splitting them apart; do not skip any of them.
tool.analyze_user_intent.title: Analyze user intent
tool.answer_from_qa.desc: Once a QA that fully answers the question is found, end the round with its answer verbatim instead of letting the AI rewrite it. The system double-checks whether that QA really answers the question in full and falls back to the normal flow when it does not.
tool.answer_from_qa.example.description: Call it only when the QA answer already answers the question in full; otherwise compose the answer yourself as usual.
tool.answer_from_qa.example.extraPrompt: Do not add your own explanation after quoting it.
tool.answer_from_qa.param.document_id: The QA document id to quote directly (must be a real id returned by search_qa this round; do not make one up)
tool.answer_from_qa.title: Answer with the QA text as-is
tool.ask_clarifying_question.desc: When a question is vague, too broad or missing a key condition, asks the user back to get the information needed instead of guessing. After the call the conversation stops and waits for the user to reply.
tool.ask_clarifying_question.example.des: When the user asks about service prices or booking but does not say which kind of pet, use this tool to ask which animal it is.
tool.ask_clarifying_question.example.ext: Ask for only the single most important condition at a time, in a friendly tone; put the common choices in options: dog, cat, rabbit, rodent.
tool.ask_clarifying_question.param.optio: Common choices offered to the user for quick picking
tool.ask_clarifying_question.param.quest: The clarifying question to ask the user (shown verbatim as this turn's reply)
tool.ask_clarifying_question.title: Ask a clarifying question
tool.calculate.desc: Evaluates math expressions (arithmetic, powers, square roots, trigonometry and so on). Numbers only, no variables.
tool.calculate.example.description: Call this when the user asks you to work out an amount, a quantity or a ratio; do not do the arithmetic in your head.
tool.calculate.example.extraPrompt: Include the expression in the reply so the user can check it.
tool.calculate.param.expression: The expression to evaluate, for example 2+3*4 or sqrt(16)
tool.calculate.title: Calculator
tool.convert_units.desc: Converts between units of the same kind (length, mass, temperature, area, volume). A cross-category conversion (metres to kilograms, say) returns an error instead of forcing out a number.
tool.convert_units.example.description: When the unit the user gives differs from the unit in our data, convert first and then answer.
tool.convert_units.example.extraPrompt: Keep one decimal place in the result, and list the original value and unit alongside it.
tool.convert_units.param.from_unit: The source unit, for example kg
tool.convert_units.param.to_unit: The target unit, for example lb
tool.convert_units.title: Unit conversion
tool.date_calculate.desc: Counts the days between two dates, adds or subtracts days, and looks up the day of the week for a date.
tool.date_calculate.example.description: Call this when the user asks how many days are left, which date something is due, or what day of the week a date was.
tool.date_calculate.example.extraPrompt: Write out the start and end dates used in the calculation.
tool.date_calculate.param.op: What to do: days_between (days apart), add_days (add or subtract days), weekday (day of the week)
tool.date_calculate.param.value: The input value for the chosen op, for example 2026-01-01,2026-03-01
tool.date_calculate.title: Date arithmetic
tool.date_tool.desc: Converts between ROC and Gregorian years, and turns wording like tomorrow or next Wednesday into an actual date.
tool.date_tool.example.description: Call this when the user mentions an ROC year, or uses relative wording such as tomorrow or next week.
tool.date_tool.example.extraPrompt: Give both the ROC and the Gregorian year after converting, so it cannot be misread.
tool.date_tool.param.op: What to do: now (current time), roc_to_ad (ROC to Gregorian), ad_to_roc (Gregorian to ROC), resolve_relative (resolve a relative date)
tool.date_tool.param.value: The input value for the chosen op, for example the ROC year 114, or next Wednesday
tool.date_tool.title: Date helper
tool.get_current_datetime.desc: Gets the date and time right now, for questions like what time is it or what is today's date. The time zone always comes from this profile's time zone setting and the AI cannot change it.
tool.get_current_datetime.example.descri: Call this only when the user asks about now, today, or anything else tied to the current time.
tool.get_current_datetime.example.extraP: State the time zone used when you reply.
tool.get_current_datetime.title: Current date and time
tool.get_document.desc: Fetches the full content of a document. The document ID must come from an earlier search result and cannot be made up.
tool.get_document.example.description: When the snippets from a search are not enough for a complete answer, fetch the full text before answering.
tool.get_document.example.extraPrompt: Fetch only the one document you actually need; do not pull back everything the search found.
tool.get_document.param.document_id: Document ID (a real value from a search result)
tool.get_document.title: Get full document
tool.list_available_datasets.desc: Lists the names and descriptions of the datasets this profile can currently search, so the AI knows which scopes it can reach.
tool.list_available_datasets.example.des: When you are unsure which data scope a question falls under, list the searchable datasets first and then decide how to search.
tool.list_available_datasets.example.ext: If the topic the user asks about is outside the searchable scope, say plainly that we have no data of that kind.
tool.list_available_datasets.title: List searchable datasets
tool.lunar.desc: Converts between the Gregorian and lunar calendars, and looks up the 24 solar terms.
tool.lunar.example.description: Call this when the user asks about a lunar date, a solar term or a traditional festival.
tool.lunar.example.extraPrompt: Include the matching Gregorian date when you reply.
tool.lunar.param.op: What to do: solar_to_lunar (Gregorian to lunar), solar_term (look up a solar term), lunar_to_solar (lunar to Gregorian)
tool.lunar.param.value: A date as YYYY-MM-DD; a four-digit year on its own is enough when listing a whole year of solar terms
tool.lunar.title: Lunar calendar and solar terms
tool.search_knowledge_base.desc: Finds content relevant to the question among this tenant's knowledge base documents. The search scope and result count come from the profile; the AI only decides what terms to search for.
tool.search_knowledge_base.example.descr: Whenever the user asks about our business, products or policies, always search the knowledge base before answering.
tool.search_knowledge_base.example.extra: Search with the user's own wording first; if nothing comes back, try other keywords rather than simply saying nothing was found.
tool.search_knowledge_base.title: Search knowledge base
tool.search_qa.desc: Looks for a matching question in the tenant's QA sets (paired questions and answers); on a hit, that answer can be used as the reply directly.
tool.search_qa.example.description: Check the QA sets first for common questions, and only search knowledge base documents when nothing matches.
tool.search_qa.example.extraPrompt: Quote the matching QA answer verbatim; do not reword it.
tool.search_qa.title: Search QA sets
tool.summarize_document.desc: Fetches the whole document and produces a summary, for documents that are too long or when the user asks for the key points of the whole thing.
tool.summarize_document.example.descript: Use this when the user asks for the key points of a whole document, or when the document is too long.
tool.summarize_document.example.extraPro: Keep the summary to five points or fewer, and cite the passage behind each point.
tool.summarize_document.param.document_i: Document ID (a real value from a search result)
tool.summarize_document.title: Summarize document
widget.intro: Embed keys let the public frontend bot tell which tenant it belongs to. Each key is locked to allowed domains and can be revoked anytime.
widget.originsHint: One per line; must be https://domain or http://domain, without a path or trailing slash.
